fixes.explanation: I know a little about patience, after all those years waiting in the back of a junk drawer. But Jesus never calls the disciples patient here. He says, “How much more valuable you are than the birds!” The point is how much they're worth.

That adds a condition Jesus never gives. The lilies don't labor or spin, and God still clothes them (Luke 12:27). Jesus says, “…how much more will He clothe you…” He never says God will clothe them only if they work.

Approval is a nice thing to want, friend. I've stood at the oven door waiting on a thumbs up from a cookie box more times than I'll admit. But Jesus doesn't say approval here. He says, “But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.” The kingdom is what He tells them to seek.

Right, baker. Jesus says, “But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.” The "things" are what He's been talking about: food, drink and clothes. He tells them to seek the kingdom, and He says these things will be added.
That's right, friend. Jesus says, “…an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.” That purse will not wear out. And in heaven, no thief approaches.

The temple is a fair guess, friend, and I'd have said it too. But Jesus never mentions the temple here. He says, “…an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.” The treasure is in heaven.

Almost, friend, but it's the other way around. Jesus says the treasure is in heaven, “…where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.” So no moth destroys it. That's what makes this purse different from the ones that wear out.

That's right, it's false. Jesus describes the treasure as “…an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.” The moth is on the list of things that don't destroy it. Jesus says no thief approaches it either.
That's it, baker. Jesus says, “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” Your heart will be right where your treasure is. So it's worth asking where yours is parked.

Worry is all over this passage, so I get the pull. But Jesus names something else in this line. He says, “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” It's your heart that will be there.
Eyes are a fair guess, friend, but Jesus doesn't use them here. His words are, “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” The word He picks is heart.
